climate.overview_html: The Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service released its CAMS Atmosphere Watch 2026 report on September 30, documenting that 34% of the global population was exposed to “extremely poor” ground-level ozone air quality between January 1 and September 15 — driven by the hottest northern-hemisphere summer in the observational record and the worst combined wildfire season ever measured, from the western US through southern Europe to Indonesia, all amplified by the Super El Niño. Against that backdrop, the IMO’s extraordinary Marine Environment Protection Committee session has convened in October 2026 to vote on the Net-Zero Framework for international shipping — after the October 2025 vote was adjourned 57–49 under US and Saudi pressure. The NOAA Climate Prediction Center’s latest ENSO Diagnostic Discussion confirms the Super El Niño remains near its historic peak with the Niño 3.4 index well above +3°C. The El Niño’s wind-shear effect has produced the remarkable result that not a single hurricane had formed in the Atlantic basin through October 2026 — one of the clearest manifestations of ENSO suppression of Atlantic tropical development in the modern record.

items.headline: CAMS Atmosphere Watch 2026: 34% of Global Population Exposed to “Extremely Poor” Ozone Air Quality Jan–Sep 2026; Asia 53%; 50% of Europeans Exposed to Poor or Worse; Wildfires and Record Heat Drive Worst Year in Satellite Record
items.summary: The Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service's annual Atmosphere Watch 2026 report, released September 30, documents that heat waves and wildfires combined with human-caused emissions in 2026 exposed one-third of the world's population to extremely high levels of ground-level ozone. Between January 1 and September 15, 34% of the global population experienced "extremely poor" ozone air quality — concentrations well above WHO exposure guidance. Asia had the highest regional exposure rate at 53%, driven largely by Southeast Asian haze and summer heat across South and East Asia. 50% of Europe's population was exposed to poor, very poor or extremely poor ozone levels, with northern Italy among the hardest-hit urban areas. North America recorded 66% of its population with "good" ozone levels, reflecting lower 2026 wildfire impacts compared to Asia and Europe. The CAMS report emphasises that ground-level ozone illustrates the direct link between climate change and air quality — it forms preferentially under high temperatures — and that 2026's compound hazard of record heat and record wildfire smoke emissions has created a health emergency of global scale. The report also documents transboundary pollution transport, with Southeast Asian haze reaching Japan and the Korean Peninsula, and North American wildfire smoke crossing the North Atlantic into Europe.

items.headline: NOAA CPC ENSO Diagnostic Discussion October 2026: Super El Niño Niño 3.4 Well Above +3°C; Forecast to Peak October–November; >90% Probability Very Strong Event Through NH Winter; Record SST Anomaly of 3.05°C on Sep 19
items.summary: The October 2026 NOAA Climate Prediction Center ENSO Diagnostic Discussion confirms the Super El Niño remains at historically unprecedented levels with the Niño 3.4 SST anomaly well above +3°C. NOAA forecasters expect the event to peak during October–November 2026 before gradually weakening, though it remains very strong (greater than +1.5°C) through the Northern Hemisphere winter. The advisory notes the Niño 3.4 index reached 3.05°C on September 19, a record single-day anomaly in the instrumental record extending to the 1950s. The Super El Niño is the dominant driver of global weather pattern anomalies currently observed: drought and fire conditions in Southeast Asia and the Maritime Continent, anomalous flooding in Southern Africa during its normally dry season, heat stress in northern Africa and northern South America, elevated Eastern Pacific cyclone activity, and severely suppressed Atlantic hurricane activity. The advisory estimates a greater than 90% probability of a very strong El Niño persisting through NH fall-winter.

items.headline: IMO MEPC Extraordinary Session October 2026: Net-Zero Framework Vote Under Way; US Threatens Tariffs on Supporting Nations; Vote 57–49 Adjourned in October 2025; First-Ever Mandatory Carbon Pricing for International Shipping at Stake
items.summary: The IMO's third extraordinary Marine Environment Protection Committee session has convened in October 2026 to vote on the Net-Zero Framework for international shipping. The October 2025 session (MEPC/ES.2) adjourned 57-49 after the Trump administration publicly opposed the framework and Saudi Arabia successfully moved to delay for one year. The NZF would establish a Global Fuel Standard reducing marine fuel GHG intensity and a Carbon Pricing Mechanism — levying a per-tonne charge on carbon-intensive fuels, with proceeds financing clean-fuel adoption in developing nations. The Trump administration has renewed its opposition, threatening tariffs, visa restrictions and port levies against nations supporting adoption; Singapore and other influential maritime states are reportedly told their NZF vote will be factored into bilateral trade negotiations. International shipping accounts for approximately 2.89% of global GHG emissions. If adopted, the NZF would be the first-ever mandatory carbon pricing mechanism for an entire international transport sector. (Updates October 1 digest item; vote is now actively under way.)

items.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season: Zero Hurricanes Through October 1 — Historic El Niño Wind-Shear Suppression; Eastern Pacific Season Tracks for Record with 19 Named Storms; Stark Basin Contrast
items.summary: As of October 1, 2026, the Atlantic basin had produced zero hurricanes for the entire hurricane season — one of the most striking ENSO suppression signals in the modern record. El Niño episodes increase vertical wind shear over the tropical Atlantic, disrupting the organized convective development that tropical cyclones require. In sharp contrast, the Eastern Pacific recorded 19 named storms through September 30, tracking toward the most active Eastern Pacific season on record. The basin-to-basin contrast — hyper-active Eastern Pacific, quiescent Atlantic — is one of the clearest ENSO signatures in the tropical cyclone dataset. The suppressed Atlantic season has prevented a repeat of the 2024 Atlantic season's devastating US landfall events. The NHC notes that while the season anomaly is highly unusual, the El Niño suppression mechanism is well understood; the combination with 2026's record warm SSTs could theoretically still support rapid development if a suitable disturbance forms before the official season end on November 30.

items.headline: State of the Climate September 2026: Strong El Niño Puts 2026 on Track for Second-Warmest Year; 35% Chance of Beating 2023 Record; Ocean Heat at New Annual Record
items.summary: Carbon Brief's monthly State of the Climate update for September 2026 presents the clearest statistical synthesis yet of the year's temperature trajectory. With August and September 2026 running well above average, 2026 is firmly on track to be the second-warmest calendar year in the instrumental record, behind only 2023. Carbon Brief estimates a 35% probability that 2026 will exceed 2023's record annual temperature — nearly double the 18% probability estimated in May 2026 as the Super El Niño first strengthened. Global land temperatures in 2026 have been running approximately 1.2°C above the El Niño-adjusted trend, suggesting contributions beyond ENSO alone. Ocean heat content in the upper 2,000 metres reached a new annual record, with the Pacific Ocean's off-equatorial heat uptake setting the stage for sustained surface temperature anomalies through 2027 even after the El Niño's peak.

major_events.name: Typhoon Surigae (JMA No. 26) — EXTRATROPICAL TRANSITION IMMINENT; ASIAN GAMES CLOSING CEREMONY OCT 4 AT RISK
major_events.status: NEAR-EXTRATROPICAL — Storm tracked northeast along the Honshu coastline October 1–2, bringing heavy rain and gusty winds to the Tokai and Kanto regions; central pressure rebounded to ~975 hPa; extratropical transition forecast October 3; Asian Games closing ceremony at Paloma Mizuho Stadium (Nagoya) on October 4 still faces risk of heavy residual rain; approximately 4,000 athletes and officials aboard the Costa Serena in Nagoya Harbour remain on precautionary alert; elevated landslide risk continues on rain-saturated Honshu soils following Typhoon Dujuan ($22.19 B, 162 deaths) one week prior
major_events.impact: Heavy rain and transport disruption across eastern Honshu October 2–3; outdoor Asian Games events under ongoing organizer review; compound flood and landslide risk elevated in mountainous Honshu; closing ceremony October 4 faces uncertain weather even post-transition; ~1.4 million students still on remote learning in parts of Chubu region

major_events.name: Hurricane Rachel (Eastern Pacific) — ACTIVE; MOVING AWAY FROM LAND
major_events.status: HURRICANE — Active Eastern Pacific tropical cyclone approximately 200 miles south of Baja California Sur as of October 1–2, moving west-northwestward at ~10 kt and intensifying over warm El Niño–enhanced waters; not threatening land; represents 19th named system of 2026 Eastern Pacific season
major_events.impact: Marine hazards for vessels in the Eastern Pacific; follows the El Niño–enhanced Eastern Pacific hurricane track away from populated land; 2026 Eastern Pacific season tracking as most active on record consistent with Super El Niño enhancement; stark contrast to zero-hurricane Atlantic season

major_events.name: 2026 Southeast Asian Haze — ACTIVE; OCTOBER UPDATE, NO LEGAL RECOURSE FOR AFFECTED NATIONS
major_events.status: ACTIVE — ASEAN Level 3 air quality alert ongoing since August 1; wet-season onset in Kalimantan and Sumatra forecast 4–6 weeks late; October 2 analysis confirms ASEAN Haze Agreement provides no binding legal recourse for affected neighbors; Indonesian authorities warn fires could continue through October or early November
major_events.impact: Health advisories across Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Philippines and Vietnam; schools on remote learning in parts of Malaysia; cloud seeding ongoing in four countries; >12 million people affected; no binding compensation mechanism exists under international law

major_events.name: 2026 Bangkok / Thailand Floods — DRAINING; RECOVERY UNDER WAY
major_events.status: RECOVERING — Bangkok Metropolitan Administration reports drainage progressing; expected largely complete within days as of October 2; 8 deaths; 52,000+ households inundated; 4,900 evacuated; worst Bangkok flooding since 2011
major_events.impact: Recovery and damage assessment ongoing across 50 Bangkok districts; hardest-hit: Lat Phrao, Bang Khen, Don Mueang; climate attribution confirms Super El Niño significantly intensified the 2026 Southeast Asian monsoon

major_events.name: 2026 Europe Wildfire Season — WINDING DOWN; NEAR-RECORD BURNED AREA
major_events.status: WINDING DOWN — 678,978 ha burned as of late September (91% above 20-year EFFIS average); France alone ~100,000 ha; very extreme fire danger easing with autumn onset; Greece, Balkans and Caucasus maintaining elevated suppression posture through early October
major_events.impact: EU uninsured losses estimated €40–60 billion; EU Climate Insurance Alliance established September 16 as direct policy response; air quality from smoke affected >100 million Europeans; season second-worst in satellite record after 2017

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Surigae is undergoing extratropical transition by October 3 after tracking northeast along Honshu’s coast on October 1–2, with the Asian Games closing ceremony at Paloma Mizuho Stadium on October 4 still facing residual heavy-rain risk. In the Eastern Pacific, Hurricane Rachel is active approximately 200 miles south of Baja California Sur and strengthening as it moves away from land — the 19th named storm of what is tracking as the most active Eastern Pacific season on record, a direct consequence of the Super El Niño. In striking contrast, the Atlantic basin produced zero hurricanes through October 2026, reflecting the Super El Niño’s historic wind-shear suppression of Atlantic tropical development. A new October 2 analysis documents that Indonesia’s wildfire haze is choking neighboring countries with no effective legal recourse available under the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution, whose enforcement mechanism lacks binding penalty authority.

items.source: WeatherNews Japan / JMA / Japan Times / Korea JoongAng Daily
items.headline: Typhoon Surigae October 2 Update: Storm Tracks Northeast Along Honshu; Extratropical Transition Forecast October 3; Asian Games Closing Ceremony October 4 Under Weather Uncertainty; Landslide Hazard on Rain-Saturated Soils
items.summary: Typhoon Surigae (JMA Typhoon No. 26) tracked northeast along the Honshu coastline on October 1–2, bringing heavy rain and gusty winds to the Tokai and Kanto regions before beginning extratropical transition. The storm's central pressure rebounded from its 955 hPa minimum to approximately 975 hPa as it moved over progressively cooler waters north and east of the Kanto coast. JMA forecasts extratropical transition for October 3, leaving the Asian Games closing ceremony at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya on October 4 facing potential heavy residual rain even after transition. Rainfall totals of 100–200 mm in 24 hours were recorded in the most-exposed areas of Honshu. Elevated landslide risk persists across mountainous regions whose soils remain saturated from Typhoon Dujuan — the costliest typhoon in Japanese history at $22.19 billion in damage and 162 deaths — just one week prior. The approximately 4,000 athletes and officials aboard the Costa Serena cruise ship in Nagoya Harbour have been on elevated precautionary alert throughout the storm's approach.

items.headline: Hurricane Rachel Active in Eastern Pacific ~200 Miles South of Baja; 2026 Eastern Pacific Season 19 Named Storms — Tracking for Record; Zero Atlantic Hurricanes; Historic El Niño Basin Contrast
items.summary: Hurricane Rachel was active approximately 200 miles south of Baja California Sur as of October 1, 2026, moving west-northwestward at approximately 10 knots and intensifying over warm El Niño-enhanced Eastern Pacific waters. Rachel is not threatening land. The 2026 Eastern Pacific hurricane season has produced 19 named storms through October 1, tracking toward the most active Eastern Pacific season on record. In stark contrast, the Atlantic basin produced zero hurricanes through October 1, 2026 — reflecting the Super El Niño's powerful vertical wind shear suppression of Atlantic tropical cyclone development. This basin-to-basin contrast — hyper-active Eastern Pacific, quiescent Atlantic — is one of the strongest ENSO signals in the tropical cyclone record and provides some relief from Atlantic hurricane risk for the US East Coast at the height of one of the most active Pacific seasons in the observational record.

items.headline: Indonesia Haze Chokes Southeast Asian Neighbors With No Legal Recourse; ASEAN Agreement Lacks Binding Penalty Mechanism; Fires Expected Through October–November; >12 Million Affected
items.summary: A new October 2 analysis documents a critical legal gap in the regional response to the 2026 Southeast Asian haze: while Indonesia's burning fires are choking more than 12 million people across Singapore, Malaysia, Brunei, Philippines and Vietnam, the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution contains no binding penalty or compensation mechanism. Indonesia ratified the agreement in 2014, but affected nations have no formal recourse under international law to demand compensation for air quality impacts, health costs or economic losses. Indonesian authorities publicly warned that fires could continue through October or early November due to the Super El Niño delaying the wet-season onset in Kalimantan and Sumatra by 4–6 weeks relative to climatology. Cloud seeding operations are ongoing across four countries. The 2026 Southeast Asian haze crisis has already exceeded 2015's event in hotspot counts, with more than 617,400 fire hotspots recorded in Indonesia as of mid-September. The legal impasse is receiving new attention as the health and economic costs accumulate to unprecedented levels.

items.headline: FEWS.NET October 2026 Global Weather Hazards: El Niño Drives Flooding in Southern Africa’s Dry Season, Heat Stress in East Africa and Hispaniola, Beneficial Rains Central America; Super El Niño Continuing to Strengthen
items.summary: FEWS.NET's October 2026 Global Weather Hazards assessment documents broad global surface weather anomalies driven by the intensifying Super El Niño. Southern Africa — normally in its dry season in October — is experiencing active flooding driven by anomalous circulation patterns directing moisture into the region against the expected seasonal signal. Northern and eastern Africa, Hispaniola and northern South America face continued abnormal heat stress, impacting food production in food-insecure zones. Central America received beneficial heavy rain. FEWS.NET notes the Super El Niño continues to strengthen and projects a greater than 90% probability of a very strong event persisting through Northern Hemisphere winter. The unusual Southern Africa dry-season flooding echoes El Niño-driven anomalies recorded during 1997–98 and 2015–16 and is among the clearest manifestations of the nonlinear regional precipitation anomalies associated with extreme ENSO events.

renewables.overview_html: The week’s landmark renewables story is the IEA Renewables 2026 annual report, released in October, documenting a record 800 GW of global renewable capacity additions in 2025 — the 23rd consecutive year of expansion records — with solar PV alone surpassing 600 GW for the first time. The IEA Electricity 2026 report finds battery storage was the fastest-growing power technology at +40% to nearly 110 GW of annual additions — exceeding the highest-ever annual additions of natural gas. On October 1, a burst of European transactions closed: Swedish solar developer Alight acquired a ~2 GW portfolio of 40 solar projects in Sweden in the largest such portfolio transaction in the country’s history; Swiss firm Fu-Gen sold a 100 MW ready-to-build standalone BESS in Finland to London-based Nala Renewables; and Turkey launched a 2.4 GW wind and solar auction with bids open from October 13.

items.headline: IEA Renewables 2026: Record 800 GW Global Capacity Additions in 2025; Solar PV Surpasses 600 GW for First Time; Battery Storage Fastest Growing Power Tech (+40% to 110 GW); 23rd Consecutive Year of Records; US Forecast Cut ~40%
items.summary: The IEA's Renewables 2026 annual flagship report documents that global renewable energy capacity additions set a new record at 800 GW in 2025 — the 23rd consecutive year of expansion records — with solar PV accounting for more than three-quarters of the total and surpassing 600 GW of additions for the first time. Battery storage was the fastest-growing power technology, rising 40% to approximately 110 GW of annual additions — exceeding the highest-ever annual natural gas additions. The report forecasts continued rapid growth through 2031, driven by falling costs, energy security imperatives and corporate procurement. However, the IEA substantially revised down its US deployment forecasts, cutting projected US solar capacity by approximately 40% and wind by nearly 60% due to policy uncertainty and tariff-related supply chain disruption. China continues to dominate global solar and wind additions, representing over 50% of the global total. The report covers solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biofuels and biogases across electricity, transport, heating and the biogases sector.

items.headline: Alight Acquires ~2 GW Swedish Solar Development Portfolio of 40 Projects; Most with Battery Storage Options; Largest Swedish Solar Portfolio Transaction on Record
items.summary: Swedish solar developer Alight acquired a renewable energy development portfolio of approximately 2 GW in Sweden on October 1, comprising 40 individual solar projects, most of which include options for co-located battery storage. The acquisition is described as the largest transaction involving a solar development portfolio in Sweden's history, significantly expanding Alight's pipeline and cementing its position as one of Sweden's largest solar developers. The Swedish market has become increasingly active for solar development following grid connection improvements and continued panel cost declines, with the country targeting significant growth in distributed and utility-scale solar to reduce seasonal dependence on hydro and nuclear.

items.headline: Fu-Gen Sells 100 MW Ready-to-Build Standalone BESS in Finland to Nala Renewables; Battery Storage Market in Nordic Region Accelerating Under High Renewables Penetration
items.summary: Swiss-based renewables developer Fu-Gen sold a 100 MW ready-to-build standalone battery energy storage system project in Finland to London-based platform Nala Renewables on October 1, 2026, as part of an ongoing strategic partnership. The ready-to-build project is positioned for rapid progression through construction financing and commissioning. The transaction reflects accelerating battery storage investment in the Nordic region, where variable renewables penetration is rising and grid operators are procuring increasing volumes of frequency regulation and balancing capacity from large-scale battery installations. Finland has attracted significant BESS investment following energy market reforms and rising wholesale power price volatility.

items.source: Industrial Info Media / Turkish Ministry of Energy
items.headline: Turkey Launches 2.4 GW Wind and Solar Auction October 2026; 1.5 GW Onshore Wind + 900 MW Solar; Bids Open October 13
items.summary: Turkey's Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources launched a 2.4 GW renewable energy auction in October 2026, allocating 1.5 GW to onshore wind and 900 MW to solar PV projects, with bids accepted from October 13. The auction is part of Turkey's accelerated renewables programme aimed at reducing dependence on imported natural gas and improving energy security. Turkey has one of Europe's largest untapped onshore wind resources and has rapidly expanded solar capacity to approximately 30 GW by mid-2026. The 2.4 GW procurement represents a significant near-term addition to Turkey's pipeline as the country pursues a target of 120 GW of total renewables by 2035.

items.headline: IEA Electricity 2026: Renewables to Overtake Coal in Global Generation in 2026; Battery Storage Fastest-Growing Power Source; Half of World’s Electricity from Renewables and Nuclear by 2030
items.summary: The IEA Electricity 2026 report, released alongside Renewables 2026, forecasts that renewable electricity generation will overtake coal-fired output globally in 2026 for the first time — a structural milestone. Global generation from renewables is forecast to grow more than 8% in 2026. Half of the world's electricity is forecast to come from renewables and nuclear combined by 2030. Battery storage is explicitly named as the fastest-growing power technology in 2026, enabling higher solar penetration by absorbing daytime surplus for evening dispatch. The US market faces the steepest downgrade of any major economy: the IEA cut its US renewables capacity projections by approximately 40% for solar and 60% for wind relative to prior forecasts, attributing the revision to tariff uncertainty and project financing risk under current US energy policy.

science.overview_html: The period’s most consequential applied AI weather advance is WeatherNext 3 (arXiv 2609.03582, September 3), Google DeepMind and Google Research’s next-generation model that produces hourly forecasts at 0.1° resolution ingesting live geostationary satellite mosaics hourly — bypassing the 6-hour observation-assembly lag common to all prior AI weather models; WN3 is now live in Google Search, Gemini, Maps and Earth Engine. Two September arXiv submissions advance precipitation science: arXiv 2609.03210 demonstrates that fine-tuning a graph-transformer with IMERG satellite precipitation data improves medium-range precipitation CRPS by up to 19%, targeting ERA5’s known precipitation bias; while Nested-EAGLE (arXiv 2608.26822) bridges short- and medium-range forecasting in one model at 6 km resolution over CONUS, outperforming GFS and HRRR for near-surface variables. The IMSI workshop “Unpacking AI Weather Emulators” concluded October 2 with consensus that benchmark evaluation systematically understates physics-based model advantages in extreme-event regimes, and that WeatherNext 3’s direct observation ingestion is the most significant architectural step toward closing the data assimilation gap.

items.headline: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv 2609.03582): Hourly Forecasts at 0.1° / ~5 km; Live Geostationary Satellite Ingestion; +50% Precipitation Accuracy; Powers Google Maps, Search, Gemini; Bypasses 6-Hour Analysis Lag
items.meta: Stephan Rasp + 23 co-authors · Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv 2609.03582
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv 2609.03582, September 3, 2026) is the most significant architectural advance in operational AI weather forecasting since GraphCast. Unlike all prior state-of-the-art AI weather models — which are initialised exclusively from analysis data (ERA5 or operational analyses) — WN3 directly ingests raw observational data: live geostationary satellite image mosaics updated every hour, plus sparse weather station measurements for 2-metre temperature and dewpoint. This eliminates the traditional 6-hour observation-assembly lag inherent in numerical analysis cycles. WN3 forecasts at 0.1° horizontal resolution (~11 km) with hourly time steps for all variables, and at approximately 5 km for single-level surface variables including solar irradiance and cloud cover — comparable to or finer than the best physics-based operational models. Precipitation accuracy improved by up to 50% over WeatherNext 2. WN3 is integrated into Google Search, the Gemini AI assistant, Google Maps via the Maps Weather API, Google Earth Engine and BigQuery for enterprise use. The TechCrunch summary notes WN3 is described as giving users "no excuse to forget their umbrella" given hourly hyperlocal updates.

items.source: Schmitt, Delorme, King, Patodia, Schneider, Sheshadri, Jain
items.headline: Fine-Tuning AI Weather Models with IMERG Satellite Precipitation Improves Medium-Range CRPS by up to 19%; Superior Skill for Tropical Storms and Drizzle; Submitted to Science; arXiv 2609.03210
items.meta: Schmitt, Delorme, King, Patodia, Schneider, Sheshadri, Jain · submitted to Science · arXiv 2609.03210
items.summary: arXiv 2609.03210 (September 2, 2026) presents a targeted solution to one of AI weather models' most persistent weaknesses: precipitation forecasting. Current global AI weather models trained on ERA5 reanalysis inherit ERA5's known precipitation biases, particularly in the tropics where in-situ observations are sparse. The authors fine-tune a graph-transformer architecture with IMERG (Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM) satellite precipitation data at 0.25° resolution, creating a model that learns precipitation distributions from satellite-retrieved observations. The resulting model improves medium-range continuous ranked probability scores by up to 19%, with particularly strong gains for tropical storm precipitation and drizzle events — the precise regimes where ERA5-trained models perform worst. The approach is applicable to any graph-transformer AI weather model and represents a low-cost path to substantially better precipitation guidance. Submitted to Science.

items.source: Smith, Pope, Frolov, Basarab, Abdi, Madden, Jankov
items.headline: Nested-EAGLE: Bridging Short- and Medium-Range Forecasting in One ML Model; 0.25° Global + 6 km CONUS Refinement; Outperforms GFS and HRRR for Near-Surface Variables; arXiv 2608.26822
items.meta: Smith, Pope, Frolov, Basarab, Abdi, Madden, Jankov · arXiv 2608.26822
items.summary: arXiv 2608.26822 (August 27, 2026) presents Nested-EAGLE (Experimental Artificial Intelligence Global and Limited-Area Ensemble), a machine learning weather model that jointly produces short-range (hours to days) and medium-range (up to two weeks) forecasts in a single unified system. Nested-EAGLE runs at 0.25° global resolution with a 6 km refinement grid over the contiguous United States, providing local detail typical of mesoscale models within a globally-consistent medium-range framework. The model achieves significantly lower mean-squared error than NOAA's Global Forecast System and High-Resolution Rapid Refresh for near-surface variables over CONUS, while remaining competitive globally. The skill gains stem from incorporating high-resolution regional analysis data into training through the nesting process — the first demonstration of this approach in an end-to-end global-to-regional ML weather model. The model is designed for operational integration into NOAA's forecasting workflow, addressing a persistent gap in US operational forecasting where global and mesoscale model guidance must be manually reconciled.

items.headline: IMSI Workshop “Unpacking AI Weather Emulators” Concludes October 2: Benchmark Bias, Physical Realism, Data Assimilation Gap and WeatherNext 3’s Observation Ingestion Debated by 80+ Researchers
items.summary: The five-day IMSI Institute workshop 'Unpacking AI Weather Emulators' concluded October 2, 2026, at the University of Chicago, following intensive sessions from September 28 that convened approximately 80 researchers from operational weather centres, AI laboratories and academic institutions. Key consensuses reached: (1) AI weather models outperform physics-based NWP on most standard metrics but exhibit physical inconsistencies at the tails of variable distributions, particularly for extreme precipitation and temperature events; (2) the benchmark evaluation landscape is systematically biased toward metrics where AI models happen to excel, understating physics-based model advantages in extreme-event regimes where forecast value is highest; (3) the path to full operational deployment requires tight integration with data assimilation — an area where all current operational AI models still depend on physics-based analysis products; (4) WeatherNext 3's direct observation ingestion represents the most significant architectural step toward closing this gap since GraphCast. A workshop report summarising areas of consensus, open questions and recommended research priorities is expected in the coming months.

items.headline: ECMWF Goes Live with IFS Cycle 50r1 and AIFS v2: Fully Coupled Ocean–Atmosphere Data Assimilation, AIFS Wave and Snow Forecasts, Discontinues External ML Models Due to Analysis-Dependency Fragility
items.summary: ECMWF implemented its most significant forecast system update in several years on May 12, 2026, simultaneously upgrading the physics-based Integrated Forecasting System to Cycle 50r1 and deploying AIFS v2. IFS Cycle 50r1 introduces fully coupled ocean–atmosphere data assimilation for the first time, substantially improving representation of convective precipitation and tropical upper-air temperature and wind forecasts. AIFS v2 adds the first ECMWF data-driven wave forecasts, additional land-surface fields, and new pressure levels in the stratosphere, expanding the set of ML-predicted variables substantially. Simultaneously, ECMWF discontinued real-time operation of externally developed ML models (including operational use of GraphCast, PanguWeather and FengWu at ECMWF) because the IFS Cycle 50r1 analysis — on which all external models are trained via ERA5 — changed sufficiently to degrade external model performance; ECMWF's own AIFS was retrained on the updated analysis and was unaffected. The episode underscores a fundamental fragility of any AI weather model trained on a fixed reanalysis: its performance is coupled to the underlying analysis system.

items.title: Verisk: Global Modeled Insured Catastrophe Losses Average $171 Billion Annually — Highest Ever Published; +$19 Billion Year-on-Year; North America $124 Billion; RMS Atlantic Hurricane Model Up 65% Since 2015
items.body_html: Verisk’s 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses report estimates that global insurers should plan for $171 billion in average annual insured catastrophe losses — a $19 billion increase from the prior year and the highest figure Verisk has ever published in the report’s 14-year history. The benchmark rose despite 2025 recording no US hurricane landfalls for the first time in a decade, reflecting continued growth in insured property values and accelerating losses from secondary perils — severe convective storms, wildfire and flood. North America accounts for $124 billion of the $171 billion global average annual loss, with Europe at $24 billion and Asia at $10 billion. The embedded RMS 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Model projects a mean annual loss of $23.4 billion — 65% higher than its 2015 predecessor, driven by rising insured coastal exposure and updated climate-adjusted storm intensification assumptions.

items.title: Artemis: Record $11.3 Billion Cat Bond Issuance in Q2 2026; H1 Total $18 Billion; Outstanding Market Hits $65.6 Billion; Wildfire Now Fastest-Growing Cat Bond Peril
items.body_html: Q2 2026 catastrophe bond issuance exceeded $11.3 billion across 48 transactions — the first quarter in market history to surpass $11 billion — with nine first-time sponsors entering the market. H1 2026 issuance reached $18 billion, exceeding H1 2025’s prior record of $17.6 billion, and the outstanding market reached a record $65.6 billion at end-Q2, having roughly doubled since 2020. Wildfire cat bonds — a category that barely existed before 2021 — are now the fastest-growing peril class, with six new wildfire structures issued in Q2 alone, as the 2026 California and European wildfire seasons validate insurers’ use of capital markets to transfer tail risk. The surge in issuance reflects systematic repricing of physical climate risk across the insurance industry.

items.title: Tomorrow.io Expands Series F to $210 Million; Pitango and Harel Insurance Add $35 Million to DeepSky AI-Native Satellite Constellation and Agentic Weather Platform
items.body_html: Weather intelligence company Tomorrow.io expanded its Series F to $210 million with a $35 million add-on from existing partners Pitango and Harel Insurance & Finance, bringing total funding past $500 million. The round originally closed in February 2026 at $175 million — led by Stonecourt Capital and HarbourVest Partners — to finance DeepSky, billed as the world’s first AI-native weather satellite constellation, completing its first generation and beginning its second. The add-on accelerates an “agentic” AI platform translating weather data into real-time operational guidance for energy, agriculture, insurance and logistics customers. Harel Insurance’s participation signals the insurance sector’s growing interest in proprietary weather data infrastructure as a hedge against catastrophe loss volatility.

items.title: NextEra’s $67 Billion Acquisition of Dominion Energy Under Regulatory Scrutiny: Virginia Governor Intervenes Over Offshore Wind Commitments; Largest US Utility M&A in History Awaiting Approval
items.body_html: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger took the unprecedented step of personally intervening in the regulatory review of NextEra Energy’s $67 billion proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy, calling herself “deeply skeptical” of the deal’s benefits for Virginia ratepayers. The acquisition, announced May 15, 2026, would create the country’s largest electric utility by combining NextEra’s ~35 GW renewables portfolio with Dominion’s flagship 6 GW Virginia offshore wind project — the largest US offshore wind development. In September 2026, the companies offered doubled bill credits (four-year duration), 1,000 new Virginia jobs and additional rate relief in an attempt to address regulatory concerns, with the full review expected to conclude in early 2027.

items.title: Plenitude Completes €1.56 Billion Capital Hike from Eni and Ares Management; Deconsolidated from Eni; Standalone Renewables Platform Accelerates Toward 15 GW Target by 2030
items.body_html: Italian renewable energy and gas-retail company Plenitude completed a €1.56 billion (approximately USD 1.76 billion) capital hike on October 1, subscribed by parent Eni SpA and Ares Management Corp, resulting in joint control and Plenitude’s deconsolidation from Eni’s consolidated financial statements. The transaction gives Plenitude greater operational and financial independence as it pursues an expanded target of 15 GW of renewables by 2030 across Italy, Spain and other European markets. Ares Management — one of the world’s largest alternative asset managers with over $450 billion AUM — brings infrastructure capital markets expertise that could support a future Plenitude IPO. Plenitude currently operates approximately 4 GW of wind and solar capacity, serves 3 million retail gas customers, and operates a growing EV charging network across Europe.
